turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My old daypack is falling apart and I've narrowed the new one down, can you help me pick?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Please wait until I've gone through all the options.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a tiny twenty litre one, super light, just enough room for water, a jacket and lunch.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then a thirty litre pack with a proper hip belt and a mesh back so you don't get a sweaty back.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And a bigger forty litre pack that would also work for overnight trips, but it's heavier and costs more.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's the last option, I'm finished. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If it's mostly day hikes, the thirty litre with the hip belt is the sweet spot. The tiny one fills up fast once you add layers, and the forty is overkill unless you really will camp.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I ask about something else? My four year old won't eat anything green. Not even peas.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Very common at that age. Hiding veg in sauces can help, but so can letting him see the green stuff over and over without pressure.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Blend spinach or courgette into a tomato pasta sauce. Grated carrot disappears in meatballs.
